- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike peaks.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in early periods (first 5–7 days); adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2–0.5 range, model tends to drift toward mean; apply mean-reversion correction: target = 0.95 * prior 14-day avg + 0.05 * current forecast.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) — model often overreacts; cap upward revisions at +2% unless sentiment >0.8.
